guide.title: 🚀 Getting started
guide.body:
Kahya has three parts: the scheduler (fires reminders), the Telegram bot (talks to you) and this panel (management).

After install, in order:
1. Settings → LLM: model name and endpoint. Running Ollama on your own machine? Use http://machine-ip:11434/v1. Using a cloud API? Enter the provider address and key.
2. Settings → Telegram: bot token (from @BotFather) and your Telegram ID, then "Send test" to verify.
3. Say "/start" to your bot in Telegram.
4. Optionally change the default password in Settings.

guide.title: 💬 Daily use via Telegram
guide.body:
Talk to Kahya naturally; it figures out whether you are recording something or asking a question.

📝 Recording examples:
• "Water bill 3000 TL arrived, due 19 august"
• "Cat Pamuk's rabies shot on september 3"
• "Remind me of rent on the 20th of every month"
• "Birthday: Ayse, march 5"
• "Customer meeting friday 2pm"
If something is missing (e.g. the date), Kahya asks; then it shows a summary card and asks for confirmation — nothing is saved without your approval.

❓ Question examples:
• "When was the rabies shot?"
• "Which bills are due this month?"
• "When was Pamuk's last vaccination?"
• "When is rent due?"

✅ Completing tasks: reply "paid" or "done" after a reminder. Repeating records (like monthly bills) roll forward automatically.

guide.title: 🎛️ Telegram commands
guide.body:
/ameleler — list ameleler
/add-amele — create an amele (wizard: name → slug → job description → confirm)
/edit-amele — change an amele's name or job description
/delete-amele — delete an amele (asks confirmation, tasks move to general)
/jobs — list open tasks
/add-job — add a task (wizard)
/done — complete the task in the reminder window
/settings — setup summary
/help — command list
/cancel — cancel a running flow

When several tasks are in the window, "/done" asks which one.

guide.title: 🤖 The amele concept
guide.body:
An amele = a role + the tasks that belong to it. In Kahya every amele is a real amele YAML file (ameleler/<slug>.yaml) — "organization as code": adding an amele is adding a file; it versioned, shareable, diffable.

When you create an amele from the panel or Telegram you only write its name and job description:
"Bill Tracker — track bills and their payment deadlines, remind 2 days before."

The system turns your description into the amele's amele system prompt. When an amele has no work, nothing runs: at due time it spawns, delivers the reminder, exits.

Amele ideas: Bill Tracker, Pet Care (vaccinations, vet), Birthday Amele, Subscription Tracker (streaming, cloud, domain renewals), Car Maintenance (inspection, oil changes), Medication Reminder, Customer Follow-up (quote deadlines, contract renewals), Warranty Tracker, Payment Plan (installments).

guide.title: 📋 Scenario library
guide.body:
• Bills: "Water bill arrives on the 20th of every month" → monthly repeat, detail 20, remind 2 days before. Reply "paid" and the next month opens automatically.
• Pets: vaccination records with yearly repeat; breed/colour/age go in the note. Ask "when was the rabies shot?"
• Birthdays: yearly repeat, detail 03-05; remind 3 days before.
• Meetings: one-off tasks; you get a "due TODAY" notice.
• Subscriptions: monthly/yearly; reminded before the renewal date.
• Car inspection: yearly repeat — never miss it.
• Installments: same day every month, with the amount — track your payment plan.
• Warranties: purchase date + warranty period; reminded before it expires.

Note: Kahya is not accounting software — it records and reminds about payments, it does not keep statutory books.

guide.title: 🛠️ LLM settings
guide.body:
Kahya works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint; it never calls a model directly — every step goes through ameles.

Local (Ollama): Settings → LLM → Endpoint: http://<machine-ip>:11434/v1, key empty. Any Ollama on your LAN works — data stays at home.

Cloud: OpenAI (https://api.openai.com/v1 + key), OpenRouter (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 + key) or another OpenAI-compatible service. The model name follows the provider (gpt-4.1-mini, openai/gpt-4.1-mini...).

Settings take effect immediately — no restart. Verify with "Test connection".

guide.title: 🔐 Privacy and data
guide.body:
Everything lives in one SQLite file: data/kahya.db. Backup = copy the file (the panel's "Download DB backup" button does exactly that).

Your data stays at home by default. One exception: Telegram messages transit Telegram's servers — that is the nature of notifications. If your LLM is cloud-based, processed texts (bill details etc.) go to that provider; with a local Ollama nothing leaves the house.

Forgot the panel password? Put KAHYA_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<password> in .env and sign in with it.

guide.title: ⚙️ Admin tips
guide.body:
• Port conflict? Change it in Settings (effective after the panel restarts).
• If the bot token changes, the bot reconnects automatically on the next message.
• The timezone setting affects reminder timing.
• The History tab shows every amele run and bot event — start debugging there.
• Running under systemd? Three units: kahya-scheduler, kahya-bot, kahya-web (examples in deploy/).
